blocks.text: [1] [Arabic, p. 125] [^n2241]And when evening came, Jesus went forth outside of the city, he and his [2] disciples. [^n2242]And as they passed in the morning, the disciples saw that fig tree [3] withered away from its root. [^n2243]And they passed by, and said, How did the fig tree dry [4] up immediately? [^n2244]And Simon remembered, and said unto him, My Master, behold, [5] that fig tree which thou didst curse hath dried up. [^n2245]And Jesus answered and said [6] unto them, Let there be in you the faith of God. [^n2246]Verily I say unto you, if ye believe, and doubt not in your hearts, and assure yourselves that that will be which [7] ye say, ye shall have what ye say. [^n2247]And if ye say to this mountain, Remove, and [8] fall[^n2248] into the sea, it shall be. [^n2249]And all that ye ask God in prayer, and believe, he [9, 10] will give you. [^n2250]And the apostles[^n2251] said unto our Lord, Increase our[^n2252] faith. [^n2253]He said unto them, If there be in you faith like a grain of mustard, ye shall say to this fig tree, Be thou torn up, and be thou planted in the sea; and it will obey you. [11] [^n2254]Who of you hath a servant driving a yoke of oxen or tending sheep, and if he [12] come from the field, will say unto him straightway, Go and sit down? [^n2255]Nay,[^n2256] he will say unto him, Make ready for me wherewith I may sup, and gird thy waist, and serve me, till I eat and drink; and afterwards thou shalt eat and drink also. [13] [^n2257]Doth that servant haply, who did what he was bid, receive his praise? I think [14] not. [^n2258]So ye also, when ye have done all that ye were bid, say, We are idle servants; what it was our duty to do, we have done.

[15] [^n2259]For this reason I say unto you, Whatever ye pray and ask, believe that ye [16] [Arabic, p. 126] receive, and ye shall have. [^n2260]And when ye stand to pray, forgive what is in your heart against any man; and your Father which is in heaven will [17] forgive you also your wrong-doings. [^n2261]But if ye forgive not men their wrong-doings, neither will your Father forgive you also your wrong-doings.

[18] [^n2262]And he spake unto them a parable also, that they should pray at all times, and [19] not be slothful: [^n2263]There was a judge in a city, who feared not God, nor was ashamed [20] for men: [^n2264]and there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, and said, [21] Avenge me of mine adversary. [^n2265]And he would not for a long time: but afterwards he said within himself, If of God I have no fear, and before men I have no shame; [22] [^n2266]yet because this widow vexeth me, I will avenge her, that she come not at all times [23, 24] and annoy me. [^n2267]And our Lord said, Hear ye what the judge of injustice said. [^n2268]And shall not God still more do vengeance for his elect, who call upon him in the night [25] and in the day, and grant them respite? [^n2269]I say unto you, He will do vengeance for them speedily. Thinkest thou the Son of man will come and find faith on the earth?

[26, 27] [^n2270]And they came again to Jerusalem. [^n2271]And it came to pass, on one of the days, as Jesus was walking in the temple, and teaching the people, and preaching the [28] gospel, [^n2272]that the chief priests and the scribes with the elders came upon him, and said unto him, Tell us: [^n2273]By what power doest thou this? and who gave thee this [29] power to do that? [^n2274]And Jesus said unto them, I also will ask you one word, and if [30] ye tell me, I also shall tell you by what power I do that. [^n2275]The baptism of John, from [31] what place is it? from heaven or of men? [^n2276]Tell me. [^n2277]And they reflected within themselves, [Arabic, p. 127] and said, If we shall say unto him, From heaven; he will say unto [32] us, For what reason did ye not believe him? [^n2278]But[^n2279] if we shall say, Of men; [33] we fear[^n2280] that the people will stone us, all of them. [^n2281]And all of them were holding[^n2282] [34] to John, that he was a true prophet. [^n2283]They answered and said unto him, We know [35] not. [^n2284]Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you also by what power I work. What think ye? A man had two sons; and he went to the first, and said unto him, My [36] son, go to-day, and till in the vineyard. [^n2285]And he answered and said, I do not wish [37] to: but finally he repented, and went. [^n2286]And he went to the other, and said unto [38] him likewise. [^n2287]And he answered and said, Yea, my lord: and went not. Which of these two did the will of his father? They said unto him, The first. Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, The publicans and harlots go before you into [39] the kingdom of God. [^n2288]John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not; but the publicans and harlots believed him; and ye, not even when ye saw, did ye repent at last, that ye might believe in him.

[40] [^n2289]Hear another parable: A man was a householder, and planted a vineyard, and surrounded it with a hedge, and digged in it a winepress, and built in it a tower, [41, 42] [^n2290]and gave it to husbandmen, and went to a distance for a long time. [^n2291]So when the time of the fruits came, he sent his servants[^n2292] unto the husbandmen, that they might [43] send him of the produce[^n2293] of his vineyard. [^n2294]And those husbandmen beat him, and [44] sent him away empty. [^n2295]And he sent unto them another servant also; and they [45] stoned him, and wounded[^n2296] him, and sent him away with shameful handling. [^n2297]And he sent again another; and they slew him. And he sent many other servants unto [46] them. [^n2298]And the husbandmen took his servants, and one they beat, and another they [47] stoned, and another they slew. [^n2299]So he sent again other servants more than the first; and [48] [Arabic, p. 128] they did likewise with them. [^n2300]So the owner of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will see him and be [49, 50] ashamed. [^n2301]So at last he sent unto them his beloved son that he had. [^n2302]But the husbandmen, when they saw the son, said amongst themselves, This is the heir. [51, 52] [^n2303]And they said, We will slay him, and so the inheritance will be ours. [^n2304]So they took [53] him, and put him forth without the vineyard, and slew him. [^n2305]When then the lord [54] of the vineyard shall come, what will he do with those husbandmen? [^n2306]They said unto him, He will destroy them in the worst of ways,[^n2307] and give the vineyard to [55] other husbandmen, who will give him fruit in its season. [^n2308]Jesus said unto them, Have ye never read in the scripture,
The stone which the builders declared to be base,
[^n2309]The same came to be at the head of the corner:
And it is wonderful in our eyes?

[57] [^n2311]Therefore I say unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and [58] given to a people that will produce fruit. [^n2312]And whosoever falleth on this stone shall be broken in pieces: but on whomsoever it falleth, it will grind him to [59] powder. [^n2313]And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they [60] perceived that it was concerning them he spake. [^n2314]And they sought to seize him; and they feared the multitude, because they were holding to him as the prophet.

n2292.text: The difference between singular and plural is very slight in Arabic.

n2296.text: A word used specially of wounding the head.
